Lina: Quick clarifying Q from todays all-hands: how should we talk about tradeoffs when customers ask "which deployment is best for us?"
Kate (CEO): Short frame: match technical constraints + economics + speed. Hosted = fastest to experiment; Dedicated = predictable throughput/cost; Private = compliance/isolation. Emphasize the decision axis, not feature lists.
Owen: Should we publish a simple decision matrix for AE/SEs? e.g., rows: latency SLO, data residency, QPS, cost predictability
Priya: Yes, and include migration notes: what it looks like to move from Hosted -> Dedicated (pin model versions, warm caches, canary traffic).
Kate (CEO): Good call. Keep the matrix one page. Include an example customer story instead of raw % claims.
Maya: On positioning vs managed cloud endpoints: customers say "we can just run endpoints on our cloud"  what's the sharp reply?
Kate (CEO): Reply: "You can build that, but it costs engineering time and leaves you with unpredictable unit economics and no inference-specific tooling. Redwood gives the primitives (autoscale, KV caching, rollouts, cost insights) so teams ship features instead of infra."
Lina: Nice. Any guidance on competitive language? avoid calling out specific vendors?
Priya: Stick to benefits and proof points. If a customer names a competitor, respond factually about differences in primitives and support model.
Kate (CEO): Also flag legal for any quant claims.
deploy-bot: All-hands slides + recording uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/1749999999 :memo:
Lina: I'll draft the decision matrix and a 2-line summary for sales. Thanks everyone!
